426:     def lookup_domain(self, domain_name, fragment):
427:         """Look up a domain by name within the design hierarchy.
428:         
429:         Args:
430:             domain_name: The name of the domain to look up
431:             fragment: The fragment context in which to look up the domain
432:             
433:         Returns:
434:             The ClockDomain object for the given domain name
435:         """
436:         # Walk up the fragment hierarchy to find the domain
437:         while fragment is not None:
438:             # Check if the domain exists in this fragment
439:             try:
440:                 if domain_name in fragment.domains:
441:                     return fragment.domains[domain_name]
442:             except TypeError:
443:                 # Handle _ModuleBuilderDomainSet case
444:                 try:
445:                     # Try to get the actual domains dict from the builder
446:                     if hasattr(fragment.domains, '_builder') and hasattr(fragment.domains._builder, '_domains'):
447:                         domains_dict = fragment.domains._builder._domains
448:                         if domain_name in domains_dict:
449:                             return domains_dict[domain_name]
450:                 except Exception:
451:                     pass
452:             # Move to the parent fragment
453:             try:
454:                 fragment = self.fragments[fragment].parent
455:             except KeyError:
456:                 # If we can't find the fragment in our map, we're done
457:                 break
458:         # Domain not found in hierarchy
459:         raise KeyError(f"Domain '{domain_name}' not found in fragment hierarchy")

461:     def _compute_fragment_depth_parent(self, fragment: Fragment, parent: "Fragment | None", depth: int):
462:         """Recursively computes every fragment's depth and parent."""
463:         self.fragments[fragment] = DesignFragmentInfo(parent, depth)
464:         for subfragment, _name, _src_loc in fragment.subfragments:
465:             self._compute_fragment_depth_parent(subfragment, fragment, depth + 1)

467:     def _use_signal(self, fragment: Fragment, signal: _ast.Signal):
468:         """Marks a signal as used in a given fragment.
469: 
470:         Also marks a signal as used if it has to be routed through a given fragment to get from
471:         one part of hierarchy to another.  For this purpose, the ``self.signal_lca`` dictionary
472:         is maintained: for every signal, it stores the topmost fragment in which it has been
473:         marked used so far.
474:         """
475:         if signal in self.fragments[fragment].used_signals:
476:             return
477:         self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
478:         if signal not in self.signal_lca:
479:             # First time we see a signal.
480:             self.signal_lca[signal] = fragment
481:             return
482:         # Signal already seen — go from current fragment to the LCA, marking everything along
483:         # the way as used.
484:         lca = self.signal_lca[signal]
485:         # First, go up from our fragment until it is no deeper than current LCA.
486:         while self.fragments[lca].depth < self.fragments[fragment].depth:
487:             fragment = self.fragments[fragment].parent
488:             # Early return if we reach a part of tree where the signal is already marked.
489:             if signal in self.fragments[fragment].used_signals:
490:                 return
491:             self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
492:         # Second, go up from current LCA until it is no deeper than our fragment.
493:         while self.fragments[lca].depth > self.fragments[fragment].depth:
494:             lca = self.fragments[lca].parent
495:             self.fragments[lca].used_signals[signal] = None
496:         # Now, both fragments are at the same depth. Go up from both until the two paths meet.
497:         while fragment is not lca:
498:             lca = self.fragments[lca].parent
499:             self.fragments[lca].used_signals[signal] = None
500:             fragment = self.fragments[fragment].parent
501:             self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
502:         self.signal_lca[signal] = lca
503: 
504:     def _use_io_port(self, fragment: Fragment, port: _ast.IOPort):

506:         frag_info = self.fragments[fragment]
507:         if port in frag_info.used_io_ports:
508:             return
509:         frag_info.used_io_ports[port] = None
510:         if frag_info.parent is not None:
511:             self._use_io_port(frag_info.parent, port)

522:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.Signal):

524:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.Operator):

526:                 self._collect_used_signals_value(fragment, op)
527:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.Slice):
528:             self._collect_used_signals_value(fragment, value.value)
529:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.Part):

532:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.SwitchValue):
533:             self._collect_used_signals_value(fragment, value.test)

536:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.Concat):

547:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.IOConcat):

553:     def _collect_used_signals_stmt(self, fragment: Fragment, stmt: _ast.Statement):

557:         elif isinstance(stmt, _ast.Print):

559:         elif isinstance(stmt, _ast.Property):

563:         elif isinstance(stmt, _ast.Switch):

565:             for _patterns, stmts, _src_loc in stmt.cases:

572:         """Collects used signals and IO ports for a fragment and all its subfragments."""
573:         from . import _mem
574:         if isinstance(fragment, _ir.Instance):

586:             if fragment.o is not None:

588:                 self._collect_used_signals_value(fragment, fragment.oe)
589:         elif isinstance(fragment, _mem.MemoryInstance):

593:                 self._collect_used_signals_value(fragment, port._en)

601:                 self._collect_used_signals_value(fragment, port._data)
602:                 self._collect_used_signals_value(fragment, port._en)
603:                 domain = fragment.domains[port._domain]
604:                 self._use_signal(fragment, domain.clk)

606:                     self._use_signal(fragment, domain.rst)
607:         else:
608:             for domain_name, statements in fragment.statements.items():
609:                 if domain_name != "comb":

611:                     self._use_signal(fragment, domain.clk)
612:                     if domain.rst is not None:
613:                         self._use_signal(fragment, domain.rst)
614:                 for statement in statements:

616:             for subfragment, _name, _src_loc in fragment.subfragments:

621:         io_ports = {conn for name, conn, dir in self.ports if isinstance(conn, _ast.IOPort)}
622:         for port in self.fragments[self.fragment].used_io_ports:

626:     def _assign_port_names(self):
627:         """Assigns names to all ports that haven't been explicitly named."""
628:         new_ports = []
629:         assigned_names = {name for name, conn, dir in self.ports if name is not None}
630:         for name, conn, dir in self.ports:
631:             if name is None:
632:                 if conn.name == "": # Nothing to name this port!
633:                     raise TypeError("Signals with private names cannot be used in unnamed top-level ports")
634:                 name = _add_name(assigned_names, conn.name)
635:                 assigned_names.add(name)
636:             new_ports.append((name, conn, dir))

639:     def _assign_names(self, fragment: Fragment, hierarchy: "tuple[str]"):
640:         """Assign names to signals and IO ports used in a given fragment, as well as its
641:         subfragments.
642: 
643:         The signal mapping is set in ``self.signal_names``, and the IO port mapping is set in
644:         ``self.io_port_names``.  Because names are deduplicated using local information only,
645:         the same signal used in a different fragment may get a different name.
646: 
647:         Subfragments may not necessarily have a name. This method assigns every such subfragment
648:         a name, ``U$<number>``, where ``<number>`` is based on its location in the hierarchy.
649: 
650:         Subfragment names may collide with signal names safely in Amaranth, but this may confuse
651:         backends. This method assigns every such subfragment a new name.
652: 
653:         Arguments
654:         ---------
655:         hierarchy : tuple of str
656:             Name of this fragment.
657:         """
658: 
659:         frag_info = self.fragments[fragment]
660:         frag_info.name = hierarchy
661: 
662:         if fragment.origins is not None:
663:             for origin in fragment.origins:
664:                 if origin in self.elaboratables:
665:                     other_hierarchy = self.fragments[self.elaboratables[origin]].name
666:                     raise DuplicateElaboratable(f"Elaboratable {origin!r} is included twice "
667:                                                 f"in the hierarchy, as {'.'.join(other_hierarchy)} "
668:                                                 f"and {'.'.join(hierarchy)}")
669:                 self.elaboratables[origin] = fragment
670: 
671:         if fragment is self.fragment:
672:             # Reserve names for top-level ports. If equal to the signal name, let the signal share it.
673:             for name, conn, _dir in self.ports:
674:                 frag_info.assigned_names.add(name)
675:                 if isinstance(conn, _ast.Signal) and conn.name == name:
676:                     frag_info.signal_names[conn] = name
677:                 elif isinstance(conn, _ast.IOPort) and conn.name == name:
678:                     frag_info.io_port_names[conn] = name
679: 
680:         for signal in frag_info.used_signals:
681:             if signal not in frag_info.signal_names and signal.name != "": # Private name shouldn't be added.
682:                 frag_info.signal_names[signal] = _add_name(frag_info.assigned_names, signal.name)
683:         for port in frag_info.used_io_ports:
684:             if port not in frag_info.io_port_names:
685:                 frag_info.io_port_names[port] = _add_name(frag_info.assigned_names, port.name)
686: 
687:         for subfragment_index, (subfragment, subfragment_name, subfragment_src_loc) in enumerate(fragment.subfragments):
688:             if subfragment_name is None:
689:                 subfragment_name = f"U${subfragment_index}"
690:             subfragment_name = _add_name(frag_info.assigned_names, subfragment_name)
691:             self._assign_names(subfragment, hierarchy=(*hierarchy, subfragment_name))

735:         self.matches_cache = {}
736:         self.priority_match_cache = {}
737:         self.fragment_module_idx: dict[Fragment, int] = {}

744:     def emit_signal(self, signal) -> _nir.Value:
745:         if signal in self.netlist.signals:
746:             return self.netlist.signals[signal]
747:         value = self.netlist.alloc_late_value(signal)
748:         self.netlist.signals[signal] = value
749:         for bit, net in enumerate(value):
750:             self.late_net_to_signal[net] = (signal, bit)

753:     def emit_io(self, value: _ast.IOValue) -> _nir.IOValue:
754:         if isinstance(value, _ast.IOPort):
755:             if value not in self.io_ports:
756:                 port = len(self.netlist.io_ports)
757:                 self.netlist.io_ports.append(value)
758:                 self.io_ports[value] = _nir.IOValue(
759:                     _nir.IONet.from_port(port, bit)
760:                     for bit in range(0, len(value))
761:                 )
762:             return self.io_ports[value]
763:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.IOConcat):
764:             result = []
765:             for part in value.parts:
766:                 result += self.emit_io(part)
767:             return _nir.IOValue(result)
768:         elif isinstance(value, _ast.IOSlice):
769:             return self.emit_io(value.value)[value.start:value.stop]

771:             raise TypeError # :nocov:

773:     def emit_io_use(self, value: _ast.IOValue, *, src_loc) -> _nir.IOValue:

782:                                      f"{prev_src_loc[0]}:{prev_src_loc[1]} and {src_loc[0]}:{src_loc[1]}")

790:             result = []

835:     def unify_shapes_bitwise(self,
836:             operand_a: _nir.Value, signed_a: bool, operand_b: _nir.Value, signed_b: bool):
837:         shape = _ast.Shape._unify((
838:             _ast.Shape(len(operand_a), signed_a),
839:             _ast.Shape(len(operand_b), signed_b),
840:         ))
841:         operand_a = self.extend(operand_a, signed_a, shape.width)
842:         operand_b = self.extend(operand_b, signed_b, shape.width)
843:         return (operand_a, operand_b, shape.signed)

845:     def emit_rhs(self, module_idx: int, value: _ast.Value) -> Tuple[_nir.Value, bool]:
846:         """Emits a RHS value, returns a tuple of (value, is_signed)"""
847:         try:
848:             result, signed, value = self.rhs_cache[id(value)]

853:             shape  = value.shape()
854:             result = _nir.Value.from_const(value.value, shape.width)
855:             signed = shape.signed

866:                 elif value.operator == 'u':
867:                     result = operand_a

869:                 elif value.operator == '-':
870:                     operand_a = self.extend(operand_a, signed_a, len(operand_a) + 1)
871:                     result = self.emit_operator(module_idx, '-', operand_a,
872:                                                 src_loc=value.src_loc)
873:                     signed = True
874:                 elif value.operator == '~':
875:                     result = self.emit_operator(module_idx, '~', operand_a,
876:                                                 src_loc=value.src_loc)
877:                     signed = signed_a
878:                 elif value.operator in ('b', 'r|', 'r&', 'r^'):
879:                     result = self.emit_operator(module_idx, value.operator, operand_a,

884:             elif len(value.operands) == 2:

886:                 operand_b, signed_b = self.emit_rhs(module_idx, value.operands[1])
887:                 if value.operator in ('|', '&', '^'):
888:                     operand_a, operand_b, signed = \
889:                         self.unify_shapes_bitwise(operand_a, signed_a, operand_b, signed_b)
890:                     result = self.emit_operator(module_idx, value.operator, operand_a, operand_b,
891:                                                 src_loc=value.src_loc)

894:                         self.unify_shapes_bitwise(operand_a, signed_a, operand_b, signed_b)

343:             self.cases.append(res)
344:         return res
345: 
346:     def default(self):
347:         res = Case(())
348:         self.cases.append(res)
349:         return res
350: 
351:     def emit(self, line):
352:         line(f"switch {self.sel}")
353:         with line.indent():
354:             for case in self.cases:
355:                 case.emit(line)
356:         line("end")

359: class Case:
360:     def __init__(self, patterns):
361:         self.patterns = patterns
362:         self.contents = []
363: 
364:     def assign(self, lhs, rhs):
365:         self.contents.append(Assignment(lhs, rhs))
366: 
367:     def switch(self, sel):
368:         res = Switch(sel)
369:         self.contents.append(res)
370:         return res
371: 
372:     def emit(self, line):
373:         if self.patterns:
374:             patterns = ", ".join(f"{len(pattern)}'{pattern}" for pattern in self.patterns)
375:             line(f"case {patterns}")
376:         else:
377:             line(f"case")
378:         with line.indent():
379:             _emit_process_contents(self.contents, line)

382: class MemoryInfo:

389: class ModuleEmitter:
390:     def __init__(self, builder, netlist: _nir.Netlist, module: _nir.Module, name_map, empty_checker):
391:         self.builder = builder
392:         self.netlist = netlist
393:         self.module = module
394:         self.name_map = name_map
395:         self.empty_checker = empty_checker
396: 
397:         # Internal state of the emitter. This conceptually consists of three parts:
398:         # (1) memory information;
399:         # (2) name and attribute preferences for wires corresponding to signals;
400:         # (3) mapping of Amaranth netlist entities to RTLIL netlist entities.
401:         # Value names are preferences: they are candidate names for values that may or may not get
402:         # used for cell outputs. Attributes are mandatory: they are always emitted, but can be
403:         # squashed if several signals end up aliasing the same driven wire.
404:         self.memories = {} # cell idx -> MemoryInfo
405:         self.value_names = {} # value -> signal or port name
406:         self.value_attrs = {} # value -> dict
407:         self.value_src_loc = {} # value -> source location
408:         self.sigport_wires = {} # signal or port name -> (wire, value)
409:         self.driven_sigports = set() # set of signal or port name
410:         self.nets = {} # net -> (wire name, bit idx)
411:         self.ionets = {} # ionet -> (wire name, bit idx)
412:         self.cell_wires = {} # cell idx -> wire name
413:         self.instance_wires = {} # (cell idx, output name) -> wire name
414: 
415:     def emit(self):
416:         self.collect_memory_info()
417:         self.assign_value_names()
418:         self.collect_init_attrs()
419:         self.emit_signal_wires()
420:         self.emit_port_wires()
421:         self.emit_io_port_wires()
422:         self.emit_cell_wires()
423:         self.emit_submodule_wires()
424:         self.emit_connects()
425:         self.emit_signal_fields()
426:         self.emit_submodules()
427:         self.emit_cells()
428: 
429:     def collect_memory_info(self):
430:         for cell_idx in self.module.cells:
431:             cell = self.netlist.cells[cell_idx]
432:             if isinstance(cell, _nir.Memory):
433:                 self.memories[cell_idx] = MemoryInfo(
434:                     self.builder.memory(cell.width, cell.depth, name=cell.name,
435:                                         attrs=cell.attributes, src_loc=cell.src_loc).name)
436: 
437:         for cell_idx in self.module.cells:
438:             cell = self.netlist.cells[cell_idx]
439:             if isinstance(cell, _nir.SyncWritePort):
440:                 memory_info = self.memories[cell.memory]
441:                 memory_info.write_port_ids[cell_idx] = memory_info.num_write_ports
442:                 memory_info.num_write_ports += 1
443: 
444:     def assign_value_names(self):
445:         for signal, name in self.module.signal_names.items():
446:             value = self.netlist.signals[signal]
447:             if value not in self.value_names:
448:                 self.value_names[value] = name
449: 
450:     def collect_init_attrs(self):
451:         # Flip-flops are special in Yosys; the initial value is stored not as a cell parameter but
452:         # as an attribute of a wire connected to the output of the flip-flop. The claimed benefit
453:         # of this arrangement is that fine cells, which cannot have parameters (so that certain
454:         # backends, like BLIF, which cannot represent parameters--or attributes--can be used to
455:         # emit these cells), then do not need to have 3x more variants (one for initialized to 0,
456:         # one for 1, one for X).
457:         #
458:         # At the time of writing, 2024-02-11, Yosys has 125 (one hundred twenty five) fine FF cells,
459:         # which are generated by a Python script because they have gotten completely out of hand
460:         # long ago and no one could keep track of them manually. This list features such beauties
461:         # as $_DFFSRE_PPPN_ and its other 7 cousins.
462:         #
463:         # These are real cells, used by real Yosys developers! Look at what they have done for us,
464:         # with all the subtly unsynthesizable Verilog we sent them and all of the incompatibilities
465:         # with vendor toolchains we reported!
466:         #
467:         # Nothing is fine about these cells. The decision to have `init` as a wire attribute is
468:         # quite possibly the single worst design decision in Yosys, and not having to dealing with
469:         # that bullshit again is enough of a reason to implement an FPGA toolchain from scratch.
470:         #
471:         # Just have 375 fine cells, bro. Trust me bro. You will certainly not regret having 375
472:         # fine cells in your toolchain. Or at least you will be able to process netlists without
473:         # having to special-case this one godforsaken attribute every time you look at a wire.
474:         #
475:         # -- @whitequark
476:         for cell_idx in self.module.cells:
477:             cell = self.netlist.cells[cell_idx]
478:             if isinstance(cell, _nir.FlipFlop):
479:                 width = len(cell.data)
480:                 attrs = {"init": _ast.Const(cell.init, width), **cell.attributes}
481:                 value = _nir.Value(_nir.Net.from_cell(cell_idx, bit) for bit in range(width))
482:                 self.value_attrs[value] = attrs
483: 
484:     def emit_signal_wires(self):
485:         for signal, name in self.module.signal_names.items():
486:             value = self.netlist.signals[signal]
487: 
488:             # One of: (1) empty and created here, (2) `init` filled in by `collect_init_attrs`,
489:             # (3) populated by some other signal aliasing the same nets. In the last case, we will
490:             # glue attributes for these signals together, but synthesizers (including Yosys, when
491:             # the design is flattened) will do that anyway, so it doesn't matter.
492:             attrs = self.value_attrs.setdefault(value, {})
493:             attrs.update(signal.attrs)
494:             self.value_src_loc[value] = signal.src_loc
495: 
496:             field = self.netlist.signal_fields[signal][()]
497:             if field.enum_name is not None:
498:                 attrs["enum_base_type"] = field.enum_name
499:             if field.enum_variants is not None:
500:                 for var_val, var_name in field.enum_variants.items():
501:                     attrs["enum_value_" + to_binary(var_val, len(signal))] = var_name
502: 
503:             if name in self.module.ports:
504:                 port_value, _flow = self.module.ports[name]
505:                 assert value == port_value
506:                 self.name_map[signal] = (*self.module.name, name)
507:             else:
508:                 shape = signal.shape()
509:                 wire  = self.builder.wire(width=shape.width, signed=shape.signed,
510:                                           name=name, attrs=attrs,
511:                                           src_loc=signal.src_loc)
512:                 self.sigport_wires[name] = (wire, value)
513:                 self.name_map[signal] = (*self.module.name, wire.name[1:])
514: 
515:     def emit_port_wires(self):
516:         named_signals = {name: signal for signal, name in self.module.signal_names.items()}
517:         for port_id, (name, (value, flow)) in enumerate(self.module.ports.items()):
518:             signed = False
519:             if name in named_signals:
520:                 signed = named_signals[name].shape().signed
521:             wire = self.builder.wire(width=len(value), signed=signed,
522:                                      port_kind=flow.value,
523:                                      name=name, attrs=self.value_attrs.get(value, {}),
524:                                      src_loc=self.value_src_loc.get(value))
525:             self.sigport_wires[name] = (wire, value)
526:             if flow == _nir.ModuleNetFlow.Output:
527:                 continue
528:             # If we just emitted an input port, it is driving the value.
529:             self.driven_sigports.add(name)
530:             for bit, net in enumerate(value):
531:                 self.nets[net] = (wire, bit)
532: 
533:     def emit_io_port_wires(self):
534:         for idx, (name, (value, dir)) in enumerate(self.module.io_ports.items()):
535:             port_id = idx + len(self.module.ports)
536:             if self.module.parent is None:
537:                 port = self.netlist.io_ports[value[0].port]
538:                 attrs = port.attrs
539:                 src_loc = port.src_loc
540:             else:
541:                 attrs = {}
542:                 src_loc = None
543:             wire = self.builder.wire(width=len(value),
544:                                      port_kind=dir.value,
545:                                      name=name, attrs=attrs,
546:                                      src_loc=src_loc)
547:             for bit, net in enumerate(value):
548:                 self.ionets[net] = (wire, bit)
549: 
550:     def emit_driven_wire(self, value):
551:         # Emits a wire for a value, in preparation for driving it.
552:         if value in self.value_names:
553:             # If there is a signal or port matching this value, reuse its wire as the canonical
554:             # wire of the nets involved.
555:             name = self.value_names[value]
556:             wire, named_value = self.sigport_wires[name]
557:             assert value == named_value, \
558:                 f"Inconsistent values {value!r}, {named_value!r} for wire {name!r}"
559:             self.driven_sigports.add(name)
560:         else:
561:             # Otherwise, make an anonymous wire.
562:             wire = self.builder.wire(len(value), attrs=self.value_attrs.get(value, {}))
563:         for bit, net in enumerate(value):
564:             self.nets[net] = (wire, bit)
565:         return wire
566: 
567:     def emit_cell_wires(self):
568:         for cell_idx in self.module.cells:
569:             cell = self.netlist.cells[cell_idx]
570:             if isinstance(cell, _nir.Top):
571:                 continue
572:             elif isinstance(cell, _nir.Instance):
573:                 for name, (start, width) in cell.ports_o.items():
574:                     nets = [_nir.Net.from_cell(cell_idx, start + bit) for bit in range(width)]
575:                     wire = self.emit_driven_wire(_nir.Value(nets))
576:                     self.instance_wires[cell_idx, name] = wire
577:                 continue # Instances use one wire per output, not per cell.
578:             elif isinstance(cell, (_nir.PriorityMatch, _nir.Matches)):
579:                 continue # Inlined into assignment lists.
580:             elif isinstance(cell, (_nir.SyncPrint, _nir.AsyncPrint, _nir.SyncProperty,
581:                                    _nir.AsyncProperty, _nir.Memory, _nir.SyncWritePort)):
582:                 continue # No outputs.
583:             elif isinstance(cell, _nir.AssignmentList):
584:                 width = len(cell.default)
585:             elif isinstance(cell, (_nir.Operator, _nir.Part, _nir.AnyValue,
586:                                    _nir.SyncReadPort, _nir.AsyncReadPort)):
587:                 width = cell.width
588:             elif isinstance(cell, _nir.FlipFlop):
589:                 width = len(cell.data)
590:             elif isinstance(cell, _nir.Initial):
591:                 width = 1
592:             elif isinstance(cell, _nir.IOBuffer):
593:                 if cell.dir is _nir.IODirection.Output:
594:                     continue # No outputs.
595:                 width = len(cell.port)
596:             else:
597:                 assert False # :nocov:
598:             # Single output cell connected to a wire.
599:             nets = [_nir.Net.from_cell(cell_idx, bit) for bit in range(width)]
600:             wire = self.emit_driven_wire(_nir.Value(nets))
601:             self.cell_wires[cell_idx] = wire
602: 
603:     def emit_submodule_wires(self):
604:         for submodule_idx in self.module.submodules:
605:             submodule = self.netlist.modules[submodule_idx]
606:             for _name, (value, flow) in submodule.ports.items():
607:                 if flow == _nir.ModuleNetFlow.Output:
608:                     self.emit_driven_wire(value)
609: 
610:     def sigspec(self, *parts: '_nir.Net | Iterable[_nir.Net]'):
611:         value = _nir.Value()
612:         for part in parts:
613:             value += _nir.Value(part)
614: 
615:         chunks = []
616:         begin_pos = 0
617:         while begin_pos < len(value):
618:             end_pos = begin_pos
619:             if value[begin_pos].is_const:
620:                 while end_pos < len(value) and value[end_pos].is_const:
621:                     end_pos += 1
622:                 width = end_pos - begin_pos
623:                 bits = "".join(str(net.const) for net in value[begin_pos:end_pos])
624:                 chunks.append(f"{width}'{bits[::-1]}")
625:             else:
626:                 wire, start_bit = self.nets[value[begin_pos]]
627:                 bit = start_bit
628:                 while (end_pos < len(value) and
629:                         not value[end_pos].is_const and
630:                         self.nets[value[end_pos]] == (wire, bit)):
631:                     end_pos += 1
632:                     bit += 1
633:                 width = end_pos - begin_pos
634:                 if width == 1:
635:                     chunks.append(f"{wire.name} [{start_bit}]")
636:                 else:
637:                     chunks.append(f"{wire.name} [{start_bit + width - 1}:{start_bit}]")
638:             begin_pos = end_pos
639: 
640:         if len(chunks) == 1:
641:             return chunks[0]
642:         return "{ " + " ".join(reversed(chunks)) + " }"
643: 
644:     def io_sigspec(self, value: _nir.IOValue):
645:         chunks = []
646:         begin_pos = 0
647:         while begin_pos < len(value):
648:             end_pos = begin_pos
649:             wire, start_bit = self.ionets[value[begin_pos]]
650:             bit = start_bit
651:             while (end_pos < len(value) and
652:                     self.ionets[value[end_pos]] == (wire, bit)):
653:                 end_pos += 1
654:                 bit += 1
655:             width = end_pos - begin_pos
656:             if width == 1:
657:                 chunks.append(f"{wire.name} [{start_bit}]")
658:             else:
659:                 chunks.append(f"{wire.name} [{start_bit + width - 1}:{start_bit}]")
660:             begin_pos = end_pos
661: 
662:         if len(chunks) == 1:
663:             return chunks[0]
664:         return "{ " + " ".join(reversed(chunks)) + " }"
665: 
666:     def emit_connects(self):
667:         for name, (wire, value) in self.sigport_wires.items():
668:             if name not in self.driven_sigports:
669:                 self.builder.connect(wire.name, self.sigspec(value))
670: 
671:     def emit_signal_fields(self):
672:         for signal, name in self.module.signal_names.items():
673:             fields = self.netlist.signal_fields[signal]
674:             for path, field in fields.items():
675:                 if path == ():
676:                     continue
677:                 name_parts = [name]
678:                 for component in path:
679:                     if isinstance(component, str):
680:                         name_parts.append(f".{component}")
681:                     elif isinstance(component, int):
682:                         name_parts.append(f"[{component}]")
683:                     else:
684:                         assert False # :nocov:
685:                 attrs = {}
686:                 if field.enum_name is not None:
687:                     attrs["enum_base_type"] = field.enum_name
688:                 if field.enum_variants is not None:
689:                     for var_val, var_name in field.enum_variants.items():
690:                         attrs["enum_value_" + to_binary(var_val, len(field.value))] = var_name
691:                 wire = self.builder.wire(width=len(field.value), signed=field.signed, attrs=attrs,
692:                                          name="".join(name_parts), src_loc=signal.src_loc)
693:                 self.builder.connect(wire.name, self.sigspec(field.value))
694: 
695:     def emit_submodules(self):
696:         for submodule_idx in self.module.submodules:
697:             submodule = self.netlist.modules[submodule_idx]
698:             if not self.empty_checker.is_empty(submodule_idx):
699:                 dotted_name = ".".join(submodule.name)
700:                 ports = {}
701:                 for name, (value, _flow) in submodule.ports.items():
702:                     ports[name] = self.sigspec(value)
703:                 for name, (value, _dir) in submodule.io_ports.items():
704:                     ports[name] = self.io_sigspec(value)
705:                 self.builder.cell(f"\\{dotted_name}", submodule.name[-1], ports=ports,
706:                                   src_loc=submodule.cell_src_loc)
707: 
708:     def emit_assignment_list(self, cell_idx, cell):
709:         def emit_assignments(case, cond):
710:             # Emits assignments from the assignment list into the given case.
711:             # ``cond`` is the net which is the condition for ``case`` being active.
712:             # Returns once it hits an assignment whose condition is not nested within ``cond``,
713:             # letting parent invocation take care of the remaining assignments.
714:             nonlocal pos
715: 
716:             while pos < len(cell.assignments):
717:                 assign = cell.assignments[pos]
718:                 if assign.cond == cond:
719:                     # Not nested, so emit the assignment.
720:                     case.assign(self.sigspec(lhs[assign.start:assign.start + len(assign.value)]),
721:                                 self.sigspec(assign.value))
722:                     pos += 1
723:                 else:
724:                     # Condition doesn't match this case's condition — either we encountered
725:                     # a nested condition, or we should break out.  Try to find out exactly
726:                     # how we are nested.
727:                     search_cond = assign.cond
728:                     while True:
729:                         if search_cond == cond:
730:                             # We have found the PriorityMatch cell that we should enter.
731:                             break
732:                         if search_cond == _nir.Net.from_const(1):
733:                             # If this isn't nested condition, go back to parent invocation.
734:                             return
735:                         # Grab the PriorityMatch cell that is on the next level of nesting.
736:                         priority_cell_idx = search_cond.cell
737:                         priority_cell = self.netlist.cells[priority_cell_idx]
738:                         assert isinstance(priority_cell, _nir.PriorityMatch)
739:                         search_cond = priority_cell.en
740:                     # We assume that:
741:                     # 1. PriorityMatch inputs can only be Match cell outputs, or constant 1.
742:                     # 2. All Match cells driving a given PriorityMatch cell test the same value.
743:                     # Grab the tested value from a random Match cell.
744:                     test = _nir.Value()
745:                     for net in priority_cell.inputs:
746:                         if net != _nir.Net.from_const(1):
747:                             matches_cell = self.netlist.cells[net.cell]
748:                             assert isinstance(matches_cell, _nir.Matches)
749:                             test = matches_cell.value
750:                             break
751:                     # Now emit cases for all PriorityMatch inputs, in sequence. Consume as many
752:                     # assignments as possible along the way.
753:                     switch = case.switch(self.sigspec(test))
754:                     for bit, net in enumerate(priority_cell.inputs):
755:                         subcond = _nir.Net.from_cell(priority_cell_idx, bit)
756:                         if net == _nir.Net.from_const(1):
757:                             emit_assignments(switch.default(), subcond)
758:                         else:
759:                             # Validate the above assumptions.
760:                             matches_cell = self.netlist.cells[net.cell]
761:                             assert isinstance(matches_cell, _nir.Matches)
762:                             assert test == matches_cell.value
763:                             patterns = matches_cell.patterns
764:                             emit_assignments(switch.case(patterns), subcond)
765: 
766:         lhs = _nir.Value(_nir.Net.from_cell(cell_idx, bit) for bit in range(len(cell.default)))
767:         proc = self.builder.process(src_loc=cell.src_loc)
768:         proc.assign(self.sigspec(lhs), self.sigspec(cell.default))
769:         pos = 0 # nonlocally used in `emit_assignments`
770:         emit_assignments(proc, _nir.Net.from_const(1))
771:         assert pos == len(cell.assignments)
772: 
773:     def shorten_operand(self, value, *, signed):
774:         value = list(value)
775:         if signed:
776:             while len(value) > 1 and value[-1] == value[-2]:
777:                 value.pop()
778:         else:
779:             while len(value) > 0 and value[-1] == _nir.Net.from_const(0):
780:                 value.pop()
781:         return _nir.Value(value)
782: 
783:     def emit_operator(self, cell_idx, cell):
784:         UNARY_OPERATORS = {
785:             "-":    "$neg",
786:             "~":    "$not",
787:             "b":    "$reduce_bool",
788:             "r|":   "$reduce_or",
789:             "r&":   "$reduce_and",
790:             "r^":   "$reduce_xor",
791:         }
792:         BINARY_OPERATORS = {
793:             #                    A_SIGNED, B_SIGNED
794:             "+":   ("$add",      False,    False),
795:             "-":   ("$sub",      False,    False),
796:             "*":   ("$mul",      False,    False),
797:             "u//": ("$divfloor", False,    False),
798:             "s//": ("$divfloor", True,     True),
799:             "u%":  ("$modfloor", False,    False),
800:             "s%":  ("$modfloor", True,     True),
801:             "<<":  ("$shl",      False,    False),
802:             "u>>": ("$shr",      False,    False),
803:             "s>>": ("$sshr",     True,     False),
804:             "&":   ("$and",      False,    False),
805:             "|":   ("$or",       False,    False),
806:             "^":   ("$xor",      False,    False),
807:             "==":  ("$eq",       False,    False),
808:             "!=":  ("$ne",       False,    False),
809:             "u<":  ("$lt",       False,    False),
810:             "u>":  ("$gt",       False,    False),
811:             "u<=": ("$le",       False,    False),
812:             "u>=": ("$ge",       False,    False),
813:             "s<":  ("$lt",       True,     True),
814:             "s>":  ("$gt",       True,     True),
815:             "s<=": ("$le",       True,     True),
816:             "s>=": ("$ge",       True,     True),
817:         }
818:         if len(cell.inputs) == 1:
819:             cell_type = UNARY_OPERATORS[cell.operator]
820:             operand, = cell.inputs
821:             signed = False
822:             if cell.operator == "-":
823:                 # For arithmetic operands, we trim the extra sign or zero extension on the operands
824:                 # to make the output prettier, and to fix inference problems in some not very smart
825:                 # synthesis tools.
826:                 operand_u = self.shorten_operand(operand, signed=False)
827:                 operand_s = self.shorten_operand(operand, signed=True)
828:                 # The operator will work when lowered with either signedness.  Pick whichever
829:                 # is prettier.
830:                 if len(operand_s) < len(operand_u):
831:                     signed = True
832:                     operand = operand_s
833:                 else:
834:                     signed = False
835:                     operand = operand_u
836:             self.builder.cell(cell_type, ports={
837:                 "A": self.sigspec(operand),
838:                 "Y": self.cell_wires[cell_idx].name
839:             }, parameters={
840:                 "A_SIGNED": signed,
841:                 "A_WIDTH": len(operand),
842:                 "Y_WIDTH": cell.width,
843:             }, src_loc=cell.src_loc)
844:         elif len(cell.inputs) == 2:
845:             cell_type, a_signed, b_signed = BINARY_OPERATORS[cell.operator]
846:             operand_a, operand_b = cell.inputs
847:             if cell.operator in ("+", "-", "*", "==", "!="):
848:                 # Arithmetic operators that will work with any signedness, but we have to choose

    def elaborate(self, platform):
        return self


class FragmentGetTestCase(FHDLTestCase):
    def test_get_wrong_none(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(TypeError,
                r"^Object None is not an 'Elaboratable' nor 'Fragment'$"):
            Fragment.get(None, platform=None)

        with self.assertWarnsRegex(UserWarning,
                r"^\.elaborate\(\) returned None; missing return statement\?$"):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(TypeError,
                    r"^Object None is not an 'Elaboratable' nor 'Fragment'$"):
                Fragment.get(ElaboratesToNone(), platform=None)

    def test_get_wrong_self(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RecursionError,
                r"^Object <.+?ElaboratesToSelf.+?> elaborates to itself$"):
            Fragment.get(ElaboratesToSelf(), platform=None)


class FragmentGeneratedTestCase(FHDLTestCase):
    def test_find_subfragment(self):
        f1 = Fragment()
        f2 = Fragment()
        f1.add_subfragment(f2, "f2")

        self.assertEqual(f1.find_subfragment(0), f2)
        self.assertEqual(f1.find_subfragment("f2"), f2)

    def test_find_subfragment_wrong(self):
        f1 = Fragment()
        f2 = Fragment()
        f1.add_subfragment(f2, "f2")

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(NameError,
                r"^No subfragment at index #1$"):
            f1.find_subfragment(1)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(NameError,
                r"^No subfragment with name 'fx'$"):
            f1.find_subfragment("fx")

    def test_find_generated(self):
        f1 = Fragment()
        f2 = Fragment()
        f2.generated["sig"] = sig = Signal()
        f1.add_subfragment(f2, "f2")

        self.assertEqual(SignalKey(f1.find_generated("f2", "sig")),
                         SignalKey(sig))


class DuplicateElaboratableTestCase(FHDLTestCase):
    def test_duplicate(self):
        sub = Module()
        m = Module()
        m.submodules.a = sub
        m.submodules.b = sub
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(DuplicateElaboratable,
                r"^Elaboratable .* is included twice in the hierarchy, as "
                r"top\.a and top\.b$"):
            Fragment.get(m, None).prepare()

class FragmentDomainsTestCase(FHDLTestCase):
    def test_propagate_up(self):
        cd = ClockDomain()

        f1 = Fragment()
        f2 = Fragment()
        f1.add_subfragment(f2)
        f2.add_domains(cd)

        f1._propagate_domains_up()
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains, {"cd": cd})

    def test_propagate_up_local(self):
        cd = ClockDomain(local=True)

        f1 = Fragment()
        f2 = Fragment()
        f1.add_subfragment(f2)
        f2.add_domains(cd)

        f1._propagate_domains_up()
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains, {})

    def test_domain_conflict(self):
        cda = ClockDomain("sync")
        cdb = ClockDomain("sync")

        fa = Fragment()
        fa.add_domains(cda)
        fb = Fragment()
        fb.add_domains(cdb)
        f = Fragment()
        f.add_subfragment(fa, "a")
        f.add_subfragment(fb, "b")

        f._propagate_domains_up()
        self.assertEqual(f.domains, {"a_sync": cda, "b_sync": cdb})
        (fa, _, _), (fb, _, _) = f.subfragments
        self.assertEqual(fa.domains, {"a_sync": cda})
        self.assertEqual(fb.domains, {"b_sync": cdb})

    def test_domain_conflict_anon(self):
        cda = ClockDomain("sync")
        cdb = ClockDomain("sync")

        fa = Fragment()
        fa.add_domains(cda)
        fb = Fragment()
        fb.add_domains(cdb)
        f = Fragment()
        f.add_subfragment(fa, "a")
        f.add_subfragment(fb)

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(DomainError,
                (r"^Domain 'sync' is defined by subfragments 'a', <unnamed #1> of fragment "
                    r"'top'; it is necessary to either rename subfragment domains explicitly, "
                    r"or give names to subfragments$")):
            f._propagate_domains_up()

    def test_domain_conflict_name(self):
        cda = ClockDomain("sync")
        cdb = ClockDomain("sync")

        fa = Fragment()
        fa.add_domains(cda)
        fb = Fragment()
        fb.add_domains(cdb)
        f = Fragment()
        f.add_subfragment(fa, "x")
        f.add_subfragment(fb, "x")

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(DomainError,
                (r"^Domain 'sync' is defined by subfragments #0, #1 of fragment 'top', some "
                    r"of which have identical names; it is necessary to either rename subfragment "
                    r"domains explicitly, or give distinct names to subfragments$")):
            f._propagate_domains_up()

    def test_domain_conflict_rename_drivers(self):
        cda = ClockDomain("sync")
        cdb = ClockDomain("sync")

        fa = Fragment()
        fa.add_domains(cda)
        fb = Fragment()
        fb.add_domains(cdb)
        fb.add_statements("comb", ResetSignal("sync").eq(1))
        f = Fragment()
        f.add_subfragment(fa, "a")
        f.add_subfragment(fb, "b")

        f._propagate_domains_up()
        fb_new, _, _ = f.subfragments[1]
        self.assertRepr(fb_new.statements["comb"], "((eq (rst b_sync) (const 1'd1)))")

    def test_domain_conflict_rename_drivers_before_creating_missing(self):
        cda = ClockDomain("sync")
        cdb = ClockDomain("sync")
        s = Signal()

        fa = Fragment()
        fa.add_domains(cda)
        fb = Fragment()
        fb.add_domains(cdb)
        f = Fragment()
        f.add_subfragment(fa, "a")
        f.add_subfragment(fb, "b")
        f.add_statements("b_sync", s.eq(1))

        f._propagate_domains(lambda name: ClockDomain(name))

    def test_propagate_down(self):
        cd = ClockDomain()

        f1 = Fragment()
        f2 = Fragment()
        f1.add_domains(cd)
        f1.add_subfragment(f2)

        f1._propagate_domains_down()
        self.assertEqual(f2.domains, {"cd": cd})

    def test_propagate_down_idempotent(self):
        cd = ClockDomain()

        f1 = Fragment()
        f1.add_domains(cd)
        f2 = Fragment()
        f2.add_domains(cd)
        f1.add_subfragment(f2)

        f1._propagate_domains_down()
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains, {"cd": cd})
        self.assertEqual(f2.domains, {"cd": cd})

    def test_propagate(self):
        cd = ClockDomain()

        f1 = Fragment()
        f2 = Fragment()
        f1.add_domains(cd)
        f1.add_subfragment(f2)

        new_domains = f1._propagate_domains(missing_domain=lambda name: None)
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains, {"cd": cd})
        self.assertEqual(f2.domains, {"cd": cd})
        self.assertEqual(new_domains, [])

    def test_propagate_missing(self):
        s1 = Signal()
        f1 = Fragment()
        f1.add_statements("sync", s1.eq(1))

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(DomainError,
                r"^Domain 'sync' is used but not defined$"):
            f1._propagate_domains(missing_domain=lambda name: None)

    def test_propagate_create_missing(self):
        s1 = Signal()
        f1 = Fragment()
        f1.add_statements("sync", s1.eq(1))
        f2 = Fragment()
        f1.add_subfragment(f2)

        new_domains = f1._propagate_domains(missing_domain=lambda name: ClockDomain(name))
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains.keys(), {"sync"})
        self.assertEqual(f2.domains.keys(), {"sync"})
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains["sync"], f2.domains["sync"])
        self.assertEqual(new_domains, [f1.domains["sync"]])

    def test_propagate_create_missing_fragment(self):
        s1 = Signal()
        f1 = Fragment()
        f1.add_statements("sync", s1.eq(1))

        cd = ClockDomain("sync")
        f2 = Fragment()
        f2.add_domains(cd)

        new_domains = f1._propagate_domains(missing_domain=lambda name: f2)
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains.keys(), {"sync"})
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains["sync"], f2.domains["sync"])
        self.assertEqual(new_domains, [])
        self.assertEqual(f1.subfragments, [
            (f2, "cd_sync", None)
        ])

    def test_propagate_create_missing_fragment_many_domains(self):
        s1 = Signal()
        f1 = Fragment()
        f1.add_statements("sync", s1.eq(1))

        cd_por  = ClockDomain("por")
        cd_sync = ClockDomain("sync")
        f2 = Fragment()
        f2.add_domains(cd_por, cd_sync)

        new_domains = f1._propagate_domains(missing_domain=lambda name: f2)
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains.keys(), {"sync", "por"})
        self.assertEqual(f2.domains.keys(), {"sync", "por"})
        self.assertEqual(f1.domains["sync"], f2.domains["sync"])
        self.assertEqual(new_domains, [])
        self.assertEqual(f1.subfragments, [
            (f2, "cd_sync", None)
        ])

    def test_propagate_create_missing_fragment_wrong(self):
        s1 = Signal()
        f1 = Fragment()
        f1.add_statements("sync", s1.eq(1))

        f2 = Fragment()
        f2.add_domains(ClockDomain("foo"))

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(DomainError,
                (r"^Fragment returned by missing domain callback does not define requested "
                    r"domain 'sync' \(defines 'foo'\)\.$")):
            f1._propagate_domains(missing_domain=lambda name: f2)

    def test_propagate_up_use(self):
        a = Signal()
        m = Module()
        m1 = Module()
        m2 = Module()
        m.submodules.m1 = m1
        m.submodules.m2 = m2
        m1.d.test += a.eq(1)
        m2.domains.test = ClockDomain()
        with self.assertWarnsRegex(DeprecationWarning,
                r"^Domain 'test' is used in 'top.m1', but defined in 'top.m2', which will not be "
                r"supported in Amaranth 0.6; define the domain in 'top' or one of its parents$"):

        design = f.prepare(ports)

class ElaboratesTo(Elaboratable):
    def __init__(self, lower):
        self.lower = lower

    def elaborate(self, platform):
        return self.lower


class OriginsTestCase(FHDLTestCase):
    def test_origins(self):
        elab1 = ElaboratesTo(elab2 := ElaboratesTo(m := Module()))
        frag = Fragment.get(elab1, platform=None)
        self.assertEqual(len(frag.origins), 3)
        self.assertIsInstance(frag.origins, tuple)
        self.assertIs(frag.origins[0], elab1)
        self.assertIs(frag.origins[1], elab2)
        self.assertIs(frag.origins[2], m)

    def test_origins_disable(self):
        inst = Instance("test")
        del inst.origins
        elab = ElaboratesTo(inst)
        frag = Fragment.get(elab, platform=None)
        self.assertFalse(hasattr(frag, "_origins"))

import os

from amaranth._utils import _ignore_deprecated


class SimulatorUnitTestCase(FHDLTestCase):
    def assertStatement(self, stmt, inputs, output, init=0):
        inputs = [Value.cast(i) for i in inputs]
        output = Value.cast(output)

        isigs = [Signal(i.shape(), name=n) for i, n in zip(inputs, "abcd")]
        osig  = Signal(output.shape(), name="y", init=init)

        stmt = stmt(osig, *isigs)
        frag = Fragment()
        frag.add_statements("comb", stmt)

        sim = Simulator(frag)
        async def process(ctx):
            for isig, input in zip(isigs, inputs):
                ctx.set(isig, ctx.get(input))
            self.assertEqual(ctx.get(osig), output.value)
        sim.add_testbench(process)
        with sim.write_vcd("test.vcd", "test.gtkw", traces=[*isigs, osig]):
            sim.run()

        frag = Fragment()
        sim = Simulator(frag)
        async def process(ctx):
            for isig, input in zip(isigs, inputs):
                ctx.set(isig, ctx.get(input))
            if isinstance(stmt, Assign):
                ctx.set(stmt.lhs, ctx.get(stmt.rhs))
            else:
                for s in stmt:
                    ctx.set(s.lhs, ctx.get(s.rhs))
            self.assertEqual(ctx.get(osig), output.value)
        sim.add_testbench(process)
        with sim.write_vcd("test.vcd", "test.gtkw", traces=[*isigs, osig]):
            sim.run()


    def test_invert(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.eq(~a)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b0000, 4)], C(0b1111, 4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b1010, 4)], C(0b0101, 4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0,      4)], C(-1,     4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b0000, signed(4))], C(-1, signed(4)))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b1010, signed(4))], C(0b0101, signed(4)))

    def test_neg(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.eq(-a)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b0000, 4)], C(0b0000, 4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b0001, 4)], C(0b1111, 4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b1010, 4)], C(0b0110, 4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(1,      4)], C(-1,     4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(5,      4)], C(-5,     4))

    def test_bool(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.eq(a.bool())
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0, 4)], C(0))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(1, 4)], C(1))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(2, 4)], C(1))

    def test_as_unsigned(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a, b: y.eq(a.as_unsigned() == b)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, signed(2)), C(0b0001, unsigned(4))], C(1))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b11, signed(2)), C(0b0011, unsigned(4))], C(1))

    def test_as_unsigned_lhs(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.as_unsigned().eq(a)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, unsigned(2))], C(0b0001, signed(4)))

    def test_as_signed(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a, b: y.eq(a.as_signed() == b)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, unsigned(2)), C(0b0001, signed(4))], C(1))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b11, unsigned(2)), C(0b1111, signed(4))], C(1))

    def test_as_signed_issue_502(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.eq(a.as_signed())
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, unsigned(2))], C(0b0001, signed(4)))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b11, unsigned(2))], C(0b1111, signed(4)))

    def test_as_signed_lhs(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.as_signed().eq(a)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, unsigned(2))], C(0b0001, signed(4)))

    def test_any(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.eq(a.any())
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b00, 2)], C(0))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, 2)], C(1))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b10, 2)], C(1))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b11, 2)], C(1))

    def test_all(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.eq(a.all())
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b00, 2)], C(0))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, 2)], C(0))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b10, 2)], C(0))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b11, 2)], C(1))

    def test_xor_unary(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a: y.eq(a.xor())
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b00, 2)], C(0))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b01, 2)], C(1))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b10, 2)], C(1))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0b11, 2)], C(0))

    def test_add(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a, b: y.eq(a + b)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0,  4), C(1,  4)], C(1,   4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(-5, 4), C(-5, 4)], C(-10, 5))

    def test_sub(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a, b: y.eq(a - b)
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(2,  4), C(1,  4)], C(1,   4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0,  4), C(1,  4)], C(-1,  4))
        self.assertStatement(stmt, [C(0,  4), C(10, 4)], C(-10, 5))

    def test_mul(self):
        stmt = lambda y, a, b: y.eq(a * b)

class SimulatorIntegrationTestCase(FHDLTestCase):
    @contextmanager
    def assertSimulation(self, module, *, deadline=None, traces=[]):
        sim = Simulator(module)
        yield sim
        with sim.write_vcd("test.vcd", "test.gtkw", traces=traces):
            if deadline is None:
                sim.run()
            else:
                sim.run_until(deadline)

    def setUp_counter(self):
        self.count = Signal(3, init=4)
        self.sync  = ClockDomain()

        self.m = Module()
        self.m.d.sync  += self.count.eq(self.count + 1)
        self.m.domains += self.sync

    def test_counter_process(self):
        self.setUp_counter()
        with self.assertSimulation(self.m) as sim:
            def process():
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 4)
                yield Delay(1e-6)
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 4)
                yield self.sync.clk.eq(1)
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 4)
                with _ignore_deprecated():
                    yield Settle()
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 5)
                yield Delay(1e-6)
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 5)
                yield self.sync.clk.eq(0)
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 5)
                with _ignore_deprecated():
                    yield Settle()
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 5)
                for _ in range(3):
                    yield Delay(1e-6)
                    yield self.sync.clk.eq(1)
                    yield Delay(1e-6)
                    yield self.sync.clk.eq(0)
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 0)
            sim.add_process(process)

    def test_counter_clock_and_sync_process(self):
        self.setUp_counter()
        with self.assertSimulation(self.m) as sim:
            sim.add_clock(1e-6, domain="sync")
            def process():
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 4)
                self.assertEqual((yield self.sync.clk), 1)
                yield
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 5)
                self.assertEqual((yield self.sync.clk), 1)
                for _ in range(3):
                    yield
                self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 0)
            with _ignore_deprecated():
                sim.add_sync_process(process)

    def test_reset(self):
        self.setUp_counter()
        sim = Simulator(self.m)
        sim.add_clock(1e-6)
        times = 0
        def process():
            nonlocal times
            yield Tick()
            self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 4)
            yield Tick()
            self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 5)
            yield Tick()
            self.assertEqual((yield self.count), 6)
            yield Tick()
            times += 1
        sim.add_process(process)
        sim.run()
        sim.reset()
        sim.run()
        self.assertEqual(times, 2)

    def setUp_alu(self):
        self.a = Signal(8)
        self.b = Signal(8)
        self.o = Signal(8)
        self.x = Signal(8)
        self.s = Signal(2)
        self.sync = ClockDomain(reset_less=True)

        self.m = Module()
        self.m.d.comb += self.x.eq(self.a ^ self.b)
        with self.m.Switch(self.s):
            with self.m.Case(0):
                self.m.d.sync += self.o.eq(self.a + self.b)
            with self.m.Case():
                self.m.d.sync += self.o.eq(self.a * self.b)
            with self.m.Case(1):
                self.m.d.sync += self.o.eq(self.a - self.b)
            with self.m.Default():
                self.m.d.sync += self.o.eq(0)
        self.m.domains += self.sync

    def test_alu(self):
        self.setUp_alu()
        with self.assertSimulation(self.m) as sim:
            sim.add_clock(1e-6)
            def process():
                yield self.a.eq(5)
                yield self.b.eq(1)
                yield Tick()
                self.assertEqual((yield self.x), 4)
                yield Tick()
                self.assertEqual((yield self.o), 6)
                yield self.s.eq(1)
                yield Tick()
                yield Tick()
                self.assertEqual((yield self.o), 4)
                yield self.s.eq(2)
                yield Tick()
                yield Tick()
                self.assertEqual((yield self.o), 0)
            sim.add_process(process)

    def test_alu_bench(self):
        self.setUp_alu()
        with self.assertSimulation(self.m) as sim:
            sim.add_clock(1e-6)
            async def process(ctx):
                ctx.set(self.a, 5)
                ctx.set(self.b, 1)
                self.assertEqual(ctx.get(self.x), 4)
                await ctx.tick()
                self.assertEqual(ctx.get(self.o), 6)
                ctx.set(self.s, 1)
                await ctx.tick()
                self.assertEqual(ctx.get(self.o), 4)
                ctx.set(self.s, 2)
                await ctx.tick()
                self.assertEqual(ctx.get(self.o), 0)
            sim.add_testbench(process)

        self.m = Module()
        self.phase0 = self.m.domains.phase0 = ClockDomain()
